paragraphs: Two Animals We Lost, posted by Mia. In the science museum, I saw a model of a dodo beside a model of a toad. Both animals are extinct, which means that none of them lives now. I love animals, so this page is special for me. Guide Ann helped me with the facts. I made a fact file for each animal. Here is the first one.

The Dodo. Size: it was about one meter tall, and it was very heavy. Food: it ate fruit and seeds from the forest. It had a big gray body and short, strong legs. Home: it lived on a small island far away in the sea. Life: it was a wild bird, but it could not fly. It made its nest on the ground, and it laid one egg.

Why did the dodo disappear? More than three hundred years ago, ships came to the port of its island. Before that day, there were no people on the island. The dodos were not afraid of people, so it was easy for the sailors. The sailors ate some dodos. Rats and dogs came from the ships, and they ate the eggs. The dodos had no way to run or to hide. Soon, there were no dodos at all.

The Golden Toad. Size: it was small, only about five centimeters long. Color: it was bright golden orange, so it looked like a small piece of gold. Home: it lived in a cool, wet forest high on a mountain. Life: it spent most of the year under the ground. It was shy, and it lived alone. In the wet season, it came out to find a partner.

Here is the latest news about this creature. No one has seen a golden toad for more than thirty years. A scientist told me, "Nature changes, and animals need safe homes." We can look after the animals that live today. Many animals are in danger now. Do you know another animal that is extinct? Which animal do you want to look after? Tell us in a message!
